title: The Banner at Khaybar
subtitle: The Prophetic Bestowal of Leadership upon Ali ibn Abi Talib and the Fall of the Citadels
summary: As several assaults upon the formidable redoubts of Khaybar met stubborn resistance, the Prophet uttered a celebrated proclamation promising the banner to a man beloved by Allah and His Messenger. The morning summons of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the healing of his ailing eyes, his strict instructions to invite before fighting, and the decisive breach of the fortifications form one of the most rigorously authenticated episodes of prophetic military history.

sections.text: As the siege of Khaybar's central fortifications dragged into its second week without a definitive breakthrough, the Muslim encampment experienced deep anxiety and fatigue. The defensive ramparts of Fort Na'im and the redoubts of Al-Natat were fiercely defended by veteran warriors, and initial probing attacks had not succeeded in breaching the primary gates. On that evening, sitting among his exhausted companions beneath the starlit northern sky, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a momentous declaration that immediately electrified the entire army:

لأُعْطِيَنَّ الرَّايَةَ غَدًا رَجُلاً يُحِبُّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ، وَيُحِبُّهُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ، يَفْتَحُ اللَّهُ عَلَى يَدَيْهِ
'Tomorrow I shall surely give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love; Allah will grant victory through his hands.' (Sahih al-Bukhari 2942, 3701; Sahih Muslim 2405)

The companions spent the entire night in eager anticipation, each of them praying and hoping that this extraordinary divine testimony would fall to his share. Umar ibn al-Khattab later testified: 'I never desired military leadership except on that single day, hoping that I might be the person described by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' When dawn broke, the warriors gathered around the Prophet, stretching their necks in expectation, each yearning to be summoned to receive the sacred standard.
The Summons of Ali and the Miraculous Healing

To the surprise of many in the gathering, the Prophet looked across the assembled ranks and asked: 'Where is Ali ibn Abi Talib?' The companions replied that Ali was suffering from severe ophthalmia (an acute and painful eye inflammation known as ramad) and was resting inside his tent, barely able to open his eyes to the morning light. The Prophet commanded: 'Send for him and bring him to me.'

When Ali was led into the Prophet's presence, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ applied his blessed saliva to Ali's inflamed eyes and supplicated to Allah on his behalf. Instantaneously, all pain and swelling vanished completely, as though Ali had never suffered any ailment whatsoever. The Prophet then placed the white banner of the expedition into Ali's hands. Ready for battle, Ali asked: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I fight them until they become like us?'
The Priority of Guidance over Conquest

The Prophet's response to Ali's question established an enduring ethical principle for Islamic warfare. He instructed him not to rush into combat, but to exhaust all peaceful avenues of guidance first:

انْفُذْ عَلَى رِسْلِكَ حَتَّى تَنْزِلَ بِسَاحَتِهِمْ، ثُمَّ ادْعُهُمْ إِلَى الإِسْلاَمِ، وَأَخْبِرْهُمْ بِمَا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ حَقِّ اللَّهِ فِيهِ، فَوَاللَّهِ لأَنْ يَهْدِيَ اللَّهُ بِكَ رَجُلاً وَاحِدًا خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَكَ حُمْرُ النَّعَمِ
'Advance gently until you enter their courtyard, then invite them to Islam and inform them of what is obligated upon them concerning the rights of Allah. For by Allah, that Allah guides through you a single person is better for you than possessing red camels.' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3701, Sahih Muslim 2406)
The Breakthrough and Fall of the Basalt Redoubts

Following the prophetic instructions, Ali marched forward with the banner and positioned himself beneath the walls of Fort Na'im. He issued the call to faith and justice, but the fortress leadership chose confrontation. Classical Seerah literature describes the emergence of Marhab, the renowned champion of Khaybar, who strode out in heavy armor reciting boastful verses challenging any warrior to single combat. Ali met him with unwavering courage, reciting in response his mother's childhood naming of him as 'Haydarah'—the fierce lion. In a swift and decisive duel, Ali struck Marhab down, sending shockwaves through the defensive ranks.

With their chief warrior defeated, the defenders wavered. Ali and the Muslim vanguard pressed the assault with intense vigor, forcing the fortress gates and breaching the perimeter defenses. The fall of Fort Na'im triggered a cascading collapse across the Al-Natat sector. Within days, Fort Al-Sa'b ibn Mu'adh and Qal'at al-Zubayr were systematically secured, yielding vital food stockpiles and catapults that were subsequently deployed against the remaining bastions of Al-Shiqq and Al-Katibah.

The authenticated narrative of the banner at Khaybar encapsulates the synthesis of spiritual nobility, physical valor, and ethical warfare that defined early Islamic history. It established that true victory arises not merely from martial prowess, but from divine assistance granted to those whose hearts are steadfast in devotion to Allah and His Messenger.

references.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
references.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH)
references.source: Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Hadith 2942 & Kitab Fada'il Ashab al-Nabi, Hadith 3701
references.notes: Primary authenticated narration of the banner, the healing of Ali's eye ailment, and the instruction that guiding one person is better than red camels.
